bull.t: ACI-7104 gains regulatory and clinical validation
bull.b: Fast Track and a cleared IND can support broader Phase 2 execution for ACI-7104. Combined with strong interim immunogenicity and tolerability, this improves development credibility, although efficacy remains unproven.

bull.t: Takeda partnership offers substantial pipeline economics
bull.b: Takeda’s global option provides non-dilutive validation and potential milestone and royalty economics. The payments could help fund development and diversify future revenue beyond internal financing.

bull.t: Low leverage limits immediate financial strain
bull.b: Low debt and modest leverage reduce immediate solvency pressure while AC Immune funds costly clinical programs. This gives management flexibility to invest in its pipeline without a significant debt-service burden.

bear.t: Persistent losses and weak operating leverage
bear.b: Persistent operating and net losses show the pipeline has not produced sustainable profitability. Revenue remains small and volatile relative to expenses, leaving future performance dependent on clinical progress and financing.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and shrinking equity cushion
bear.b: Cash generation reverted to substantial operating and free-cash burn after positive 2024 performance. Combined with a sharply reduced equity base, this signals recurring funding needs and potential dilution risk.

bear.t: Clinical-stage model has limited revenue visibility
bear.b: Without commercial products, funding depends on partnerships and development-contingent payments. These receipts can be uneven, while trial setbacks could delay milestones, limiting revenue visibility over the next several years.
